activity_context.topic_title: The Rank-Nullity Theorem in Terms of Linear Transformations

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Rank or Nullity of a Linear Transformation Given a Description of the Image or Kernel
examples.problem: Find $\text{nullity}(\mathbf{T})$ given that $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$ and $\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})=\{ [ x, y, z ]^T \, : \, x=y=z\}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Any vector from $\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ x \\ x\end{aligned}]=x{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})=\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{v}_1\}.$ Therefore, $\textrm{rank}(\mathbf{T})=1.$ 

Finally, according the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T) & =3-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =3-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Consider a linear transformation $T:{R}^{6}\to {R}^{6}.$ If $\text{nullity}(T)=2$ then $\text{rank}(T)=$
feedback.worked_solution:
According to the rank-nullity theorem, if $T:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n},$ then

$$
\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T)=n.
$$

For the given transformation, we have $n=6.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T) & =n \\ \text{rank}(T)+2 & =6 \\ \text{rank}(T) & =6-2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
